refused_attachments: These attachments of the e-mail were not taken (type not accepted or over the limit)

reason.sender_mismatch: Sender is not part of the ticket
reason.sender_not_verified: Sender not verified (no passing SPF / DKIM / DMARC for the From domain)
reason.no_reply_token: Ticket number in the subject without the reply address

admin.title: Inbound e-mail
admin.lead: E-mails to the support address open tickets or are added to an existing ticket as replies; suspicious ones wait in quarantine.
admin.disabled_note: Tickets by e-mail are switched off. Turn them on in the settings.
admin.empty_text: Incoming e-mails are listed here as they are processed.
admin.attachments_not_kept: Attachments of quarantined messages are not kept; only their names are listed.
admin.release_for_client: The ticket is opened for the client “{name}”.
admin.release_as_guest: The sender belongs to no client; a guest ticket is opened.
admin.discard_confirm: Discard the message? Its content is removed for good.
admin.append_hint: The sender is not one of this ticket's people. Add the message to the ticket only if you know who wrote it.
admin.appended: The message was added to the ticket.
admin.released: The message was turned into a ticket.
admin.no_sender: The message has no sender; it cannot become a ticket.
admin.settings_lead: Bring support e-mails into tickets with a Mailgun inbound route or the raw e-mail endpoint.
admin.policy_hint: For new messages from addresses that belong to no client.
admin.department_hint: Used when the recipient matches no department's e-mail address.
admin.key_set: Stored — type a new one to replace it
admin.key_hint: The “HTTP webhook signing key” under Settings → API Security in Mailgun. Stored encrypted, never shown again.
admin.trust_spf_hint: Turn on only when the Mailgun domain’s spam filter is set to “Mark spam with MIME headers”. Mail then counts as sent by a client only with X-Mailgun-Spf: Pass for an envelope sender of the From domain. Without it, mail from client addresses is treated like mail from unknown senders.
admin.authserv_hint: For the raw endpoint: the authserv-id your receiving mail server writes into Authentication-Results (it must remove forged copies of that header). Mail counts as sent by a client only with dmarc, dkim or spf = pass for the From domain in that header. Empty: no sender is verified.
admin.mailgun_help: Create a Mailgun route for your support address (and its plus addresses) with forward() to the URL below. The URL ends in “mime”, so the message arrives raw.
admin.raw_help: Send the message as is from your own mail server: the body is the raw RFC 5322 message, with an Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Optionally pass the envelope recipient as ?recipient=.
admin.token_once: This token is shown only now; copy it somewhere safe.
admin.token_replace_confirm: Create a new token? The old one stops working at once.
admin.token_delete_confirm: Delete the token? The endpoint will refuse requests.
admin.bad_key: The key looks invalid (at least 16 characters, no spaces).
admin.bad_authserv: The authserv-id may contain only letters, digits, dots and hyphens.
admin.bulk_discard_confirm: Discard the selected messages? Their content is removed for good.
